description.text: The Group has a history dating back almost 170 years to the family enterprise of Thomas James Smith who opened a small pharmacy in Hull, UK, in 1856. Following his death in 1896, his nephew Horatio Nelson Smith took over the management of the business. By the late 1990s, Smith+Nephew had expanded into being a diverse healthcare company with operations across the globe, producing various medical devices, personal care products and traditional and advanced wound care treatments. In 1998, Smith+Nephew announced a major restructuring to focus management attention and investment on three global business units – Advanced Wound Management, Endoscopy and Orthopaedics – which offered high growth and margin opportunities. In 2024, Smith+Nephew announced its current structure comprising three global business units, Advanced Wound Management, Sports Medicine and ENT and Orthopaedics. You can read more about our business units on pages 39 to 52. Smith+Nephew was incorporated and listed on the London Stock Exchange in 1937 and in 1999 the Group was also listed on the New York Stock Exchange. In 2001, Smith+Nephew became a constituent member of the FTSE 100 index in the UK. This means that Smith+Nephew is included in the top 100 companies traded on the London Stock Exchange measured in terms of market capitalisation. Today, Smith+Nephew is a public limited company incorporated and headquartered in the UK and carries out business around the world.

about.description_short: Smith+Nephew is a portfolio medical technology business focused on the repair, regeneration and replacement of soft and hard tissue. We exist to restore people's bodies and their self-belief by using technology to take the limits off living. We call this purpose 'Life Unlimited'. Our 17,000 employees deliver this mission every day, making a difference to patients' lives through the excellence of our product portfolio, and the invention and application of new technologies across our three global business units of Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine & ENT and Advanced Wound Management. Founded in Hull, UK, in 1856, we now operate in around 100 countries, and generated annual sales of $6.2 billion in 2025. Smith+Nephew is a constituent of the FTSE100 (LSE:SN, NYSE:SNN). The terms 'Group' and 'Smith+Nephew' are used to refer to Smith & Nephew plc and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context requires otherwise.

analysis_md:
# SNN — Smith & Nephew plc
Engine 5.4.0 run, 2026-10-18. UK medical-technology group filing on Form 20-F (FY ended 2025-12-31, filed 2026-03-16); traded in the US as ADSs on NYSE. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed. Per-share figures are per ADS (see ADS_RATIO_APPLIED) unless stated per ordinary share.

## What it is
Diversified medtech in 100+ countries across three franchises: Orthopaedics (hip/knee implants, trauma & extremities, CORI robotics), Sports Medicine & ENT (arthroscopy, joint repair) and Advanced Wound Management (ALLEVYN dressings, PICO single-use negative-pressure therapy, SANTYL bioactives). FY2025 revenue $6,164M (+6.1% reported YoY, key_numbers.md / financials_history.csv). Market cap: the engine's $25.37B estimate multiplies the per-ADS price by the ordinary share count; on the ADS basis (price ÷ 2 × 877,724,845 ordinary shares outstanding) the cap is roughly $12.8B — in scope under $40B either way.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (20-F via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $1,285,000,000; capex $433,000,000 (the filer's combined PP&E + intangibles purchase tag); SBC $43,000,000 (always a real cost, and small here — ~3% of OCF).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $809,000,000 = $0.9267 per ordinary share = $1.8534 per ADS** (dcf_numbers.json base_oe_latest_per_share, ADS-scaled).
- The maintenance definition is not printed in the computed outputs for this filer (oe_maintenance is blank in financials_history.csv), so no maintenance figure is quoted.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years, but the path was a deep trough and recovery: OE/share (per ordinary share) $0.4875 (2021), $0.0802 (2022), $0.1627 (2023), $0.6461 (2024), $0.9267 (2025). Net debt $2,554,000,000 = 2.26x normalized OE (diagnostics), plus lease liabilities $216,000,000.
- **Base used = normalized median of the last 3 fiscal years: $0.6461 per ordinary share = $1.2922 per ADS** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share). The FY is ~9.6 months stale and this is an IFRS/20-F filer, so ttm.py cannot build a TTM base (it reads us-gaap only and exited non-zero for SNN: no us-gaap annual facts) — the median base stands, per the worker spec. H1 2026 interim evidence (company 6-K half-year report, 4 Aug 2026) is consistent with a recovering, not collapsing, base: revenue $3,097M (+4.6% reported, +2.3% underlying), trading profit $566M (+8.1%), trading margin 18.3%, free cash flow $231M — but no filing-direct TTM OE is available, so none is pinned.

## ADS ratio — applied, and it mattered
The preliminary run priced per-ordinary-share OE against the per-ADS price and printed a meaningless weighted IRR of 5.5%. judgment.json carries `ads_ratio = {ratio: 2, source: Form 20-F FY2025 (filed 2026-03-16) registered ADS class / Exhibit 2(d), corroborated by the FY2025 results announcement's dividend of 24.1c per ordinary share = 48.2c per ADS and the company's stated 14 October 2014 ratio change to one ADS = two ordinary shares}`. The engine scaled all per-share figures x2 (flag ADS_RATIO_APPLIED). Note the trap in the older literature: pre-2014 sources say 1 ADS = 5 ordinary shares — that ratio is dead. Even after the correct x2 scaling, the verdict below does not change tier.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: leading positions and real switching friction, but returns on capital have not cleared the cost of capital through the cycle and the margin trend is adverse.
- FOR: #2 global positions in sports medicine and advanced wound care; top 3–4 in orthopaedic reconstruction, sold in 100+ countries; proprietary platforms and materials (OXINIUM implants, CORI handheld robotics, PICO single-use NPWT, ALLEVYN dressings, REGENETEN bioinductive implant); surgeon training, clinical evidence and installed instrument sets create real switching friction; three-franchise diversification balances weakness in any one segment.
- AGAINST: the `roic_proxy` series in fundamentals.json ran 7.1% (2021), 5.6% (2022), 4.9% (2023), 7.0% (2024), 8.1% (2025) — below or near the cost of capital through the cycle; the company's own >10% post-tax ROIC is only a 2026 target and 12–13% a 2028 target. Gross margin (fundamentals.json) eroded from 74.0% (2019) and 70.4% (2021) to 68.0% (2025) on pricing pressure, mix and China volume-based procurement. Larger rivals' robotics ecosystems (Stryker Mako, Zimmer ROSA, DePuy VELYS) outscale CORI, and US knee implants lost ground in 2026 (Q2 2026 US knee revenue −7.2%, per the H1 2026 report coverage). Hospitals and GPOs have high bargaining power and demand proven cost-effectiveness.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — engine 5.4.0 final run (2026-10-18)
**Growth-start sanity check (mandatory):** the engine blend is 6.15% (rev CAGR 5y 6.21%, 3y 5.73%, latest rev YoY 6.09%; the 138.55% OE/share CAGR 2y component is a trough-recovery artifact and the median blend correctly ignores it). Recent prints are softer than the blend on an underlying basis: H1 2026 underlying revenue +2.3%, Q2 2026 underlying +1.6%, and in August 2026 management cut FY2026 underlying revenue growth guidance to ~4% (from ~6%) on weak US knee demand, while guiding H2 2026 to 5.0–5.5% and keeping ~$800M free-cash-flow and >10% ROIC guidance; the RISE strategy targets a 6–7% revenue CAGR and 9–10% trading-profit CAGR by 2028, with a $500M buyback announced May 2026 supporting per-share growth. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated with offsets −0.10 / −0.05 / −0.01 / +0.03 / +0.07 vs the blend, to −3.85% / +1.15% / **+5.15%** / +9.15% / +13.15%: base sits between the soft current underlying prints and the guided H2 / RISE path; bull ≈ the RISE trading-profit CAGR; super bull (13.15%) requires full RISE delivery plus buyback shrinkage — the preliminary default super-bull start of 18.15% had no support in any print and was cut for that written reason. Bear weight was widened (probabilities 15/30/30/17/08 vs the 10/25/30/25/10 default) for the OE_VOLATILE flag and the guidance cut. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 — note even the super-bull multiplier on the median base (1.25 × $1.2922 = $1.62/ADS) sits below the latest filed FY OE of $1.8534/ADS, so the scenario stack is conservative on base level as well as growth. Price $29.06 per ADS (nasdaq_quote_api).

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | −3.85% | 0.75 | US knee share loss spreads; China VBP and GPO pricing bite; OE falls back toward the trough | $6.10 | 4.93% |
| Bear | 30% | 1.15% | 0.90 | Guidance-cut world persists: low-single-digit growth, no margin recovery | $9.02 | 6.33% |
| Base | 30% | 5.15% | 1.00 | H2-guided recovery holds; mid-single-digit growth, gradual margin rebuild | $11.83 | 7.69% |
| Bull | 17% | 9.15% | 1.10 | RISE delivered: trading-profit CAGR at target, buyback shrinks the count | $15.36 | 9.34% |
| Super bull | 8% | 13.15% | 1.25 | Full RISE over-delivery plus robotics share gains | $20.56 | 11.62% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $11.42 (−60.7% vs price), IV@12% $15.15, IV@10% $19.30, weighted IRR 7.52%, base-case IRR 7.69%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** (bear D, bull D — no band). Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 4.45%, terminal value 18.5% of IV@15%, scenario spread 3.37x, net debt 2.26x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended ~10 months ago): ttm.py was run and exited non-zero — it reads us-gaap only and SNN is an IFRS 20-F filer with no 10-Qs, so no filing-direct TTM base exists; the normalized median base is used and stated, per spec. H1 2026 interim results (revenue +4.6% reported, trading profit +8.1%, FCF $231M) were checked for a directional break and show recovery continuing, not a break either way.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years — actually >11x trough to peak, $0.0802 in 2022 to $0.9267 in 2025 per ordinary share): real. The 2022–23 trough was an operating-cash-flow collapse ($468M OCF in 2022 on a $783M working-capital build in financials_history.csv, 12-Point Plan restructuring) followed by a working-capital and margin recovery. Handled by the normalized median base (not the peak latest FY) and by widening bear-side probability to 45% (super bear + bear).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income vs OCF differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): explained, and it does not contaminate the base, which is OCF-based. Net income is depressed by non-cash charges that OCF adds back — amortisation and impairment of acquisition intangibles ($87M in H1 2026 alone, per the half-year report), restructuring and rationalisation costs, and in 2025 the ~$200M non-cash inventory provision for portfolio rationalisation under RISE (company announcement, 8 Dec 2025) — plus working-capital swings (ΔNWC −$320M in 2025 vs +$814M in 2024 in financials_history.csv). FY2025: net income $625M vs OCF $1,285M.
- **ADS_RATIO_APPLIED** (x2.0): see the ADS section above — ratio sourced from the filer's own 20-F and results announcements; the older 1 ADS = 5 shares ratio (pre-October 2014) is obsolete and was not used.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY OE/share $1.8534/ADS vs 3-yr median $1.2922/ADS): the median is the conservative one, not the distorted one in the dangerous direction — the 3-year window (2023: $0.3253/ADS, 2024: $1.2922/ADS, 2025: $1.8534/ADS, ADS-scaled from financials_history.csv) still contains the trough-recovery year 2023. The latest FY is the cleaner current run-rate but likely flattered by the 2025 working-capital release. The median is kept as the base; the method range below shows the verdict survives on the latest-FY base too.
- Preliminary-run flags **HIGH_NET_DEBT** (4.5x) and **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.5x) were artifacts of the unscaled per-ordinary-share base: on the correct ADS basis net debt is 2.26x normalized OE and the spread is 3.37x. Leverage is still real ($2,554M net debt plus $216M leases against a trough-scarred OE history) and is part of why the bear weight is 45%; confidence is low regardless.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is how far the price sits above every defensible path: even the super-bull case (13.15% growth start, 1.25x OE) values the ADS at $20.56 @15%, below the $29.06 price, and even re-running the stack on the latest-FY base ($1.8534/ADS instead of the $1.2922 median) would raise the weighted IV@15% materially but still leave it far below the $29.06 price — still a Tier D. The D is not a base-choice artifact.
- Quality is middling, not broken: OE positive 5/5 years, SBC trivial, gross margin still 68%, trading margin recovering (18.3% in H1 2026, FY2025 trading profit +15.5% per company reporting), and management is returning cash ($500M buyback). The problem is the price capitalises the RISE 2028 targets (6–7% revenue CAGR, 12–13% ROIC) as if delivered, while the filing history shows ROIC of 4.9–8.1% and a guidance cut two months ago.
- Risks to the bearish verdict: a takeout (SNN is a perennial rumoured target for larger medtech), faster CORI/LANDMARK adoption, or RISE margin delivery ahead of plan. Risks to the company: US knee share, China VBP pricing, tariff exposure, and the inventory-rationalisation programme slipping.
- Margin of safety: there is none at $29.06 on these numbers. The ADS clears a 15% hurdle only at or below the weighted IV@15% of $11.42; it clears 10% only below $19.30.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.52% on the normalized median ADS base; bear and bull cases both D; the verdict is robust to using the latest-FY base instead)
- Confidence: **Low** (IFRS filer with no filing-direct TTM, an OE history spanning >11x trough-to-peak, and a 3.37x scenario spread — but the gap to the price is so wide that no plausible input change reaches Tier C)
- One-liner: Diversified medtech with #2 positions in sports medicine and advanced wound care, moat 5/10 — Tier D: weighted IRR 7.5%, weighted IV@15% $11.42 vs $29.06 per ADS on the normalized median base ($1.29/ADS); even the super-bull IV@15% ($20.56) sits below the price, and the ADS clears 15% only at or below $11.42.
